issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int on SealSaloon, but the solution implements this functionality as a static method named computeMealCost(Meal). Additionally, the solution's Main calls calculateTotalPrice(...) while SealSaloon defines computeMealCost(...). The template Main also uses computeMealCost(...). This name/signature mismatch across problem, template, and solution is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method they must implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name/signature across all artifacts. Rename the solution's computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (or change the problem statement and all Main calls to computeMealCost) so that the method name matches the UML/specification and Main/test code. Ensure the method remains static and returns int as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's cost, but the solution implements this functionality as computeMealCost(Meal) and the template's example Main calls computeMealCost. This inconsistent naming (calculateTotalPrice vs. computeMealCost) breaks the direct mapping from the specification to the implementation and example usage, creating confusion for students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename computeMealCost(Meal) in SealSaloon to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (static, returning int) and update all call sites (Main and any examples) to call calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require computeMealCost instead, but keeping calculateTotalPrice is recommended to match the spec.
